projects.title: Appointment Schedule
projects.short: Appointment scheduler using simple website and n8n with Google Sheets.

blocks.text: Appointment Scheduler  - Website Application & Workflow Automation

Project Category: Web Application | AI Automation & Integration
Technologies: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, FastAPI, n8n, Webhooks, Google Sheets

The Appointment Scheduler is to automate the process of storing customer information from the submitted appointment.
The project combines  website with an automated backend workflow.

This demonstrate how website application can communicate with external automation services to reduce manual data entry and improve business operations.

Customers can fill out an appointment form, submit their information, and have their data automatically forwarded through an n8n workflow and stored in Google Sheets.

Development Process
1. Frontend Development
The project started with building the customer-facing appointment scheduler using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The frontend provides an interface where customers can enter their personal information and appointment details. The form was designed to collect the required information and prepare it for submission through an HTTP POST request.

2. Backend and Server Configuration
After completing the initial frontend, I configured the local development servers and backend environment. FastAPI was used as the backend/API component, while the self-hosted n8n instance handled the automation workflow. An external tunnel was configured to make the locally hosted n8n webhook accessible to the website during development.

3. n8n Workflow Development
The next step was creating an automation workflow in n8n.
I configured a Webhook node to receive incoming HTTP requests from the appointment scheduler. The workflow was designed to receive the submitted appointment information and forward the data to Google Sheets.

4. Website-to-Automation Integration
After configuring the webhook, I connected the frontend to the external n8n endpoint. The website used JavaScript HTTP POST requests to send customer information to the webhook. During integration, I also configured Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) to allow the browser to communicate with the external service.
The initial connection was successfully established, allowing the website to communicate with the n8n workflow.

5. Google Sheets Integration
Once the webhook was receiving requests, I configured Google Sheets as the destination for submitted appointment records. The n8n workflow was connected to the spreadsheet, allowing incoming customer information to be automatically inserted into the corresponding columns. This eliminated the need to manually copy and transfer submitted appointment information.

6. Testing and Troubleshooting
During development, I encountered several configuration and integration errors involving the webhook, server connection, and Google Sheets workflow. Rather than treating these errors as setbacks, I used them as opportunities to test and refine the system.

In summary:
The website successfully sent HTTP POST requests.
The n8n webhook received the submitted information.
The workflow correctly forwarded the data.
Google Sheets stored each new appointment record.

The Appointment Scheduler demonstrated of an automated data submission pipeline:
Customer → Website Application → n8n Webhook → Google Sheets

Every submitted appointment was automatically received and forwarded to the spreadsheet without requiring manual data entry.
The project demonstrates the practical integration of frontend development, backend services, webhooks, workflow automation, and data sheet.

Skills Demonstrated:
-Frontend development using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
-Backend and API configuration using FastAPI
-HTTP POST request implementation
-Webhook configuration and integration
-n8n workflow development
-Google Sheets API integration
-CORS configuration
-External tunnel configuration
-Server management and troubleshooting
-End-to-end application testing

Project Reflection
This project shows how independent technologies can work together to create a functional business solution.

Project Status:
Initial integration completed and successfully tested in a development environment.

projects.title: Email Automation System
projects.short: Built an AI-Powered Email Automation System that connects a website form to n8n. It automatically collects customer inquiries, saves submissions to Google Sheets, uses an AI Agent to generate personalized email responses, and sends them through Gmail.
projects.long:
Project Category: Web Application | AI Automation & Integration
Technologies: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, FastAPI, n8n, Webhooks, Google Sheets, Gmail, AI Agent, Render, GitHub Pages, Tunneling

Project Overview
The Email Automation System is designed to automate the process of collecting customer inquiries, storing submitted information, and generating automated email responses using personalized email responses using AI by modifying prompt instruction ensuring that generated emails align with their communication style and business requirements.

The project combines a web-based email inquiry form with an automated backend workflow powered by FastAPI and n8n. 
It allows customers to submit their email addresses and messages through a website, while the automation system processes the information, saves customer records to Google Sheets, and generates personalized email responses using an AI Agent.

It's main reason is to reduce manual email handling, streamline customer communication, and help businesses respond to customer inquiries more efficiently.

blocks.text:
Development Process
1. Frontend Development
The project started with developing a customer-facing email inquiry form using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The frontend provides an interface where customers can enter their email addresses and messages. JavaScript handles form submission and sends the collected information through an HTTP POST request to the backend.
The form serves as the entry point of the entire automation pipeline.

2. Self-Hosted n8n and External Tunnel Configuration
After developing the frontend, I configured a self-hosted n8n instance to manage the automation workflows.
To make the locally hosted n8n application accessible externally, I configured a tunneling service that exposes the local server through a public endpoint.
This allowed external applications, including the deployed website and backend services, to communicate with the n8n webhook.

3. FastAPI Backend Configuration
FastAPI was introduced as the backend/API component responsible for handling communication between the deployed frontend and the n8n automation service.During development, I encountered connectivity issues caused by network and DNS configurations involving the proxy environment. I troubleshooted the connection, tested the webhook endpoint, and updated the FastAPI configuration to use the correct n8n webhook URL. This established the communication between the website, backend, and automation workflow.

4. Website Deployment and Integration
After completing the initial frontend and backend integration, I pushed the website source code to GitHub and deployed the frontend using GitHub Pages. The deployed website was then tested to verify whether submitted customer information could reach the backend and trigger the n8n workflow. During testing, I discovered that the deployed frontend required the correct backend endpoint configuration to communicate with the automation service. After updating the FastAPI server configuration and webhook path, the website successfully submitted information to the n8n workflow.

5. Google Sheets Integration
Once the webhook successfully received customer inquiries, I integrated Google Sheets into the n8n workflow.
A Google spreadsheet was created to serve as the centralized storage for customer information. The workflow was configured to automatically forward submitted email addresses and messages to the spreadsheet. Each new form submission created a corresponding record, eliminating the need to manually copy customer information into a spreadsheet.

6. AI Agent Configuration and Prompt Engineering
The next stage involved implementing an AI Agent to generate automated email responses. I configured the AI Agent with a prompt template that guides it in understanding customer inquiries and generating appropriate email replies. The system was designed to produce structured outputs containing the information required for email delivery. I also configured a Structured Output Parser to ensure the AI Agent generated responses following the expected schema.
During implementation, I encountered parameter and schema validation errors. I troubleshooted these issues and refined the output configuration until the AI Agent successfully generated the required response structure.

7. Gmail Integration and Automated Responses
After successfully generating structured AI responses, I integrated Gmail into the n8n workflow. The Gmail node was configured to use the customer's submitted email address as the recipient and send the AI-generated response automatically. This completed the automated email response process:A customer submits an inquiry through the website.
The backend forwards the submitted information to n8n. Google Sheets stores the customer's email address and message.
The AI Agent analyzes the inquiry and generates a response.
Gmail automatically sends the generated response to the customer.


8. Production Testing and Troubleshooting
After completing the workflow configuration, I conducted several tests to verify the entire system. I encountered additional issues while testing the deployed production environment, particularly involving communication between the frontend, backend, and n8n webhook.
I continued troubleshooting and validating the integrations to ensure the automation worked beyond the local development environment.
The testing process helped verify the complete data flow, from website submission to spreadsheet storage and automated email delivery.

The project demonstrates an integrated automation pipeline:
Customer → Website Form → FastAPI Backend → n8n Webhook → Google Sheets → AI Agent → Gmail → Customer

Each component performs a specific function while communicating with the other services to complete the automation process.


Skills Demonstrated

-Frontend development using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
-Backend API development using FastAPI
-HTTP POST request implementation
-Webhook configuration and integration
-Self-hosted n8n deployment and workflow development
-External tunneling configuration
-Google Sheets integration and automated data storage
-AI Agent configuration and prompt engineering
-Structured Output Parser configuration
-Gmail API integration and automated email delivery
-GitHub repository management and GitHub Pages deployment
-Render deployment and backend configuration
-Network, DNS, and proxy troubleshooting
-Production environment testing
-End-to-end application integration

Project Reflection
This project provided practical experience in connecting independent technologies to build a functional AI-powered business solution.
Rather than simply generating AI responses, the system demonstrates how AI and with the context of how you want to respond can be integrated into an existing business communication process.

By combining frontend development, backend services, workflow automation, data storage, and email integration, the project demonstrates how repetitive customer communication tasks can be automated.

The implementation also strengthened understanding of API communication, webhooks, structured AI outputs, deployment environments, and troubleshooting distributed applications.

Development:
End-to-end integration implemented and tested, including frontend submission, Google Sheets storage, AI-generated responses, and Gmail delivery. 

Project Status: 
Production testing and further reliability improvements remain ongoing.
